newsitem.title: USA: Two more Fidelity fund managers leave.
newsitem.headline: Two more Fidelity fund managers leave.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said over the weekend that two more mutual fund managers have decided to leave the company to take jobs at other firms.

Larry Greenberg, who managed about $22 billion of assets in four funds, including Fidelity Growth Company Fund and Fidelity Emerging Growth Company Fund, and Andrew Offit, who managed the $7 billion Fidelity VIP Equity Income Fund, have both left, a spokeswoman said Saturday.
David O'Leary, president of Fidelity watchers Alpha Equity Research, said the loss of Greenberg is an especially tough blow to Fidelity.
"(Greenberg) is probably the largest manager of Nasdaq money in the United States," O'Leary said. "What I hear is that he had been asking Fidelity for preferential treatment on the trading desk."
Greenberg primarily trades technology shares and other stocks that trade on the Nasdaq market, O'Leary said.

But Fidelity's massive size -- and regulations that keep a single institition from buying more than 15 percent of the outstanding shares of a company -- have forced him to compete with other Fidelity funds in buying shares of Nasdaq companies, O'Leary said.
"I don't think they're leaving because of money. I think they're leaving because their performance is bad and they're blaming Fidelity" in not being able to trade freely, he said.
Over the past year, a large number of fund managers have either left Fidelity or been assigned to other non-managerial positions within Fidelity.
O'Leary counts about 20 managers in all at the company managing about $185 billion in assets.
